known_facts.physics_engine_api: Uses ApplyForceToCenter, ApplyLinearImpulse, world.Step (likely PyBullet or Box2D wrapper)
known_facts.action_space_continuous_support: Code supports continuous mode where action is clipped to [-1, +1]
known_facts.wind_turbulence: Optional stochastic forces applied if enable_wind is true
known_facts.fuel_constraint: Fuel is infinite per description, but optimization goal includes minimizing fuel spent

inferred_facts.state_normalization_x: Normalized to [-1, 1] relative to viewport center (0 is pad center)
inferred_facts.state_normalization_y: Normalized relative to helipad height and viewport
inferred_facts.engine_power_discrete: Main engine power fixed at 1.0 in discrete mode; Side engines fixed at 1.0
inferred_facts.landing_pad_location: Coordinates (0,0) in world space corresponds to state[0] approx 0
inferred_facts.success_termination_trigger: Likely triggered by 'not self.lander.awake' after soft landing contact
reward_inputs_available: m_power (main engine power used this step)
s_power (side engine power used this step)

uncertain_facts.game_over_definition: Whether 'self.game_over' includes successful landing or only crashes
uncertain_facts.awake_threshold: Exact velocity/angular velocity threshold for lander to go to sleep
uncertain_facts.physics_constants: Values of MAIN_ENGINE_POWER, SCALE, VIEWPORT_W are hidden in imports/constants
uncertain_facts.success_reward_logic: How 'compute_reward' distinguishes success from failure upon termination

task_goal.primary_objective: Land at the pad (0,0) as fast as possible with least fuel spent

available_inputs.state: 8-dimensional numpy array [x_norm, y_norm, vx_norm, vy_norm, angle, ang_vel_norm, leg_contact_0, leg_contact_1]
available_inputs.m_power: Float representing main engine power applied in current step (0.0 or 1.0 in discrete)
available_inputs.s_power: Float representing side engine power applied in current step (0.0 or 1.0 in discrete)
available_inputs.terminated: Boolean indicating if episode ended this step

action_space.configured_or_inferred_action_space: Discrete [0, 3] per task description; Code supports Continuous [-1, 1]^2

action_semantics.discrete_2: Fire main engine (thrust downwards relative to lander)

termination_modes.description: Lander X coordinate exceeds viewport limits
Physics object stopped moving (could be soft landing or crash)

success_like_ending.description: Lander touches down gently on pad and stops moving

signals.velocity: Low absolute values in state[2], state[3]

failure_like_endings.hard_landing: Leg contact with high velocity (inferred from state)

successful_trajectory_phases.expected_behavior: Reduce Y position, align X to 0, correct angle to upright
successful_trajectory_phases.reward_design_implication: Should reward progress towards target coordinates and orientation

successful_trajectory_phases.expected_behavior: Reduce velocity to near zero while maintaining contact
successful_trajectory_phases.reward_design_implication: Should penalize high velocity at contact and reward termination via 'not awake'

behaviors_not_to_overpenalize_early: High fuel consumption during initial correction maneuvers
likely_bad_local_optima: Crashing immediately if crash penalty is lower than time/fuel cost of flying
Hovering indefinitely near ground if time step cost is zero or negative reward for landing is too high
behavior_trajectory_prior.exploration_implications_for_initial_rew: Initial reward should encourage descent and orientation correction without punishing fuel usage too harshly to allow learning basic control

use_with_caution: terminated flag (does not distinguish success/failure alone)
state[6], state[7] (Contact can be crash or landing)

reward_design_risks: Reward hacking by oscillating near ground to avoid 'not awake' termination if not properly penalized
Ambiguity in 'game_over' flag requiring state inspection to distinguish crash from success
Time step cost missing from inputs requires internal counter maintenance
reward_hacking_risks: Agent might learn to crash immediately if negative reward for crash is small compared to cumulative time/fuel penalty
Agent might hover indefinitely if landing penalty outweighs time cost
Agent might exploit 'not awake' condition by crashing hard enough to stop physics simulation
minimum_recommended_reward_components: Positive reward for successful termination (inferred from state at termination)
